title: Smoke Without A Room
subject: an apartment emptied of furniture
caption: Trip hop in the Bristol tradition, with a modern revival edge. A dusty swung breakbeat sampled from vinyl, upright bass, a muted trumpet answering the vocal, a Rhodes playing two chords, continuous crackle. A smoky female alto sings very close to the mic, breathy and understated, never raising her voice, with a whispered double an octave down. Lo-fi intimacy, no bright highs, tape hiss throughout. 86 BPM, A minor. Late, hollow, beautiful.
lyrics:
[Intro - Breakbeat]

[Verse 1]
The sofa left a rectangle
Cleaner than the rest of the floor
Eight years of not moving anything
Printed on the carpet

[Pre-Chorus]
I keep walking into rooms
To look at nothing

[Chorus]
It's smoke without a room now
It's a shape where a thing used to be
I could paint over all of it
But then I'd have to pick a colour

[Verse 2]
Your key still opens the door
I checked, I don't know why
The lock doesn't know anything's changed
Lucky lock

[Trumpet Solo]

[Chorus]
It's smoke without a room now
It's a shape where a thing used to be
I could paint over all of it
But then I'd have to pick a colour

[Outro]
Lucky lock
Lucky lock
